earlier_scan.note: No separate Wares language found in any survey per Glottolog; village speaks Mawes [mgk]; no documentation.

sources.note: Nothing on stress; pronouns, 21 basic-vocabulary items and 6 sentences from Foley 2018 (pp. 497-8) and Voorhoeve 1975, none marked for stress.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212 (section 2.4.12 Mawes).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Total documentation of Mawes = 'ca 250 words and 15 sentences'; wordlists in Galis 1955 (20 words), Voorhoeve 1975 (40), Smits & Voorhoeve 1994; 250 words + 15 sentences to appear in Wambaliau 2006. No phonological description is mentioned.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Entry 199 WARES (classification '?'): 'The only information is from Oosterwal (1961). Culturally, the Wares speakers belong to the Tor River tribes.. we may expect Wares also to belong to this family.' Entry 90 MAWES lists villages 'Mawes Wares, Mawes Dai'; the 40-item Mawes wordlist (col. 90, source Anceaux) carries no stress or accent marks; the word 'stress'/'accent' does not occur in the text.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid mawe1251 Mawes (page + our source list ref list)
sources.note: Nothing; Mawes has 0 descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) references in Glottolog, only overviews and wordlists (Galis 1955, van der Leeden 1954, Voorhoeve 1975, Smits & Voorhoeve 1994, Hammarström 2010).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid ware1254 'Unattested: Wares' (Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank), justification text
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Verbatim: 'no separate Wares language has been found in old or recent surveys (van der Leeden 1954, Smits & Voorhoeve 1994, Grace 1956, Wambaliau 2006) -- in particular, the only language found at the village Wares, is that covered in the entry Mawes [mgk]. Since there is no data and no intelligibility information on the Wares language, we cannot assert that they spoke language different from all others.'
